import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length1_69/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length1_69/training_1.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Perform the join on 'city' as specified
df_joined = pd.merge(df0, df1, on="city", how="inner")

# Ensure columns are in the target schema order and types:
# Target Schema: ['city': string, 'driver_count': integer, 'type': string, 'date': string, 'fare': float, 'ride_id': integer]

# Convert types explicitly
df_joined['city'] = df_joined['city'].astype(str)
df_joined['driver_count'] = df_joined['driver_count'].astype(int)
df_joined['type'] = df_joined['type'].astype(str)
df_joined['date'] = df_joined['date'].astype(str)
df_joined['fare'] = df_joined['fare'].astype(float)
# ride_id looks like a large integer stored as int64 or possibly string, convert to int
df_joined['ride_id'] = df_joined['ride_id'].astype(int)

# Reorder columns to match target schema
df_target = df_joined[['city', 'driver_count', 'type', 'date', 'fare', 'ride_id']]

# Write the result to the specified path without the index
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_69/target_multisource.csv"
df_target.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
